title: Who is wise, who is rich
hook: who is wise? one who learns from everyone; who is rich? one content with their portion (Pirkei Avot 4:1)
tomorrow: if the whole earth full of wealth were yours, would it save you?

segments.voice: A week of old voices. The Japji's last verse: air, water, earth. Simon the Just's three pillars. Hillel's if not now, when. Shammai's cheerful face. Don't judge until you reach their place. And where no one is being a person, be one. Yesterday's line: be a person.
screen: `BE A PERSON.` → `A WEEK OF OLD VOICES.`

segments.voice: Quiz shows crown whoever knows the most. Ben Zoma, a sage in Pirkei Avot, ran a different quiz. Who is wise? One who learns from every person. Who is mighty? One who masters their own impulse. Who is rich? One who is glad with their portion. Who is honored? One who honors others. Four questions, and every answer turns the prize inside out. Wisdom isn't what you've stored up; it's who you're willing to learn from.
screen: `WHOEVER KNOWS THE MOST?` → `WHO IS WISE?` → `ONE WHO LEARNS FROM EVERY PERSON.`

segments.voice: The Talmud shows Ben Zoma living it. He stood on a step on the Temple Mount and looked at the crowd, and said: blessed is the one who created all these to serve me. That sounds proud until he explains. Think how hard the first human worked for bread: plowing, sowing, reaping, threshing, grinding, kneading, baking. And I wake up and find it ready. All the trades come to my door. So the crowd wasn't a nuisance to him. It was a room full of people whose work fed and clothed him, every one with something to teach. The same page of the Talmud gives a blessing for seeing a great crowd of Israel: blessed is the one who knows the secrets, because no two minds in it are alike. That's the teaching. In Judaism even a crowd gets a blessing, and wisdom starts by noticing who you owe.
screen: `BEN ZOMA ON THE STEP.` · `ALL THE TRADES COME TO MY DOOR.` · `A BLESSING FOR A CROWD.` · then, large: `LEARN FROM EVERYONE.`

segments.voice: Take one thing near you, a cup, a shirt, a piece of bread, and count, on your fingers, the hands it passed through to reach you: the grower, the maker, the driver, the shelf stocker. Pick one of them, and ask what their work could teach you.
Who is wise: Ben Zoma's question, and his answer, one who learns from every person.
Keep this one: learn from everyone, the crowd included. Six sayings, one whole week, done.

screen: `DAY 1477 COUNTS.` → `SAYINGS OF THE FATHERS · 6 OF 6.` → `TOMORROW: IF THE WHOLE EARTH'S WEALTH WERE YOURS, WOULD IT SAVE YOU?`
